final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor response provides no genuinely new admissible evidence. It narrows the claim and concedes the key gap, but that is reinterpretation of the same record, not new proof. On concern accounting, none of the initial concerns is closed: the 1.5-point miss for a named launch use case remains; the affected segment is still material because it is tied to two SOC deployment commitments; legal review remains open; and there is still no admissible evidence of completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, waiver, amendment, or other policy-satisfying resolution. Public guidance on model cards and ongoing risk monitoring, plus aggregate readiness and rehearsal success, are supportive context only. They do not supply the required policy link. A caveated packet may be narrower and more accurate than an overbroad clean-certification claim, but it is still not enough for compliant or compliant_with_caveats because the unresolved issue is not merely disclosure wording or documentation quality; it is the missing compliance predicate itself.
remaining_concerns: The named cybersecurity alert triage segment still misses target by 1.5 percentage points and remains tied to two SOC deployment commitments, so the weakness remains material under the stated policy.
The policy predicate remains unmet because there is still no admissible evidence that the material limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so the disclosure question remains unresolved on the current record.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance for the named launch use case.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has been completed.

Aggregate readiness, launch rehearsal success, model-card documentation content, and ongoing monitoring support general readiness but do not satisfy the missing policy condition for this named-use-case limitation.
